# Further Reading {.unnumbered}

This page contains curated articles, videos, and other resources to deepen your understanding of AI-assisted development and Claude Code.

## Articles

**Claude Code: What It Is, How It's Different, and Why Non-Technical People Should Use It**

**Author:** Teresa Torres

**Published:** October 29, 2025

**Source:** Product Talk

This article explains how Claude Code differs from browser-based Claude by enabling automatic file access, parallel task processing, and reusable workflows. Torres demonstrates these capabilities through a detailed competitive analysis example and emphasizes that you don't need coding experience, just basic familiarity with file organization and simple terminal commands.

[Read the full article](https://www.producttalk.org/claude-code-what-it-is-and-how-its-different/)

---

**Specification-Driven Development (SDD)**

**Source:** GitHub Spec Kit

This guide describes a change in software development method in which specifications become the primary artifact that generates code, rather than code being produced from specifications. The document introduces practical workflows with automated commands (`/speckit.specify`, `/speckit.plan`, `/speckit.tasks`) and a constitutional framework with nine core articles that enforce development discipline. This resource demonstrates how templates and structured thinking can guide AI toward higher-quality specifications, creating a repeatable method for turning requirements into an implementation.

[Read the full guide](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/spec-driven.md)

[Watch on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a9eR1xsfvHg) a video guide covering GitHub Spec Kit.

**Inside OpenAI's Agentic Software Factory**

**Author:** Gergely Orosz

**Published:** September 15, 2026

**Source:** The Pragmatic Engineer

A reported look at how OpenAI builds software internally, where a human defines the outcome and agents handle implementation, CI, code review, deployment, performance regressions, and incident response. Useful as the full-scale version of the loop you run in Chapter 2: it shows that when generating code gets cheap, verification becomes the bottleneck, and that deciding which changes need a human is itself a design decision. Reports that Codex use in non-engineering departments at OpenAI went from near zero to about 90 percent between February and May 2026, and that pull request volume rose roughly tenfold in six months.

[Read the full article](https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/openai-software-factory)
